rounds.prompt: Someone has left a message on my desk.

options.text: Someone has been left by a message.
A message has been left on my desk.
I left a message on someone else's desk.

rounds.explanation: The present perfect passive is «has been left».

rounds.prompt: People believe that the bridge is unsafe.

options.text: The bridge is believed to be unsafe.
The bridge is believing to be unsafe.
People are believed the bridge unsafe.

rounds.explanation: The subject of the belief becomes the subject of «is believed to be».

rounds.prompt: “I will send the details tonight,” Carla said.

options.text: Carla said that she would send the details that night.
Carla told that she will send the details tonight.
Carla said she sent the details yesterday.

rounds.prompt: The school built a new sports hall last year.

options.text: The sports hall has built the school.
A new hall built the school last year.
A new sports hall was built by the school last year.

rounds.explanation: The object becomes the subject of the past passive «was built».

rounds.prompt: I started working from home six months ago.

options.text: I work from home since six months.
I have worked from home since six months.
I have worked from home for six months.

rounds.explanation: A duration from the past to now uses «have worked ... for six months».

rounds.prompt: Someone should check the figures before publication.

options.text: Someone should be checked by the figures.
The figures should be checked before publication.
The figures were checking before publication.

rounds.explanation: The modal passive is «should be checked».

rounds.prompt: The last time I used a paper map was in 2018.

options.text: I did not use a paper map in 2018.
I have not used a paper map since 2018.
I use a paper map since 2018.

rounds.explanation: The last occurrence sets the starting point of a negative present-perfect period.

rounds.prompt: The instructions were so complicated that nobody finished quickly.

options.text: They were such complicated instructions that nobody finished quickly.
They were such a complicated instructions that nobody finished.
The instructions were so a complicated that nobody finished.

rounds.explanation: The adjective moves before the plural noun after «such».

rounds.prompt: Someone delivers the letters every morning.

options.text: Someone is delivering one letter now.
The letters deliver the postman.
The letters are delivered every morning.

rounds.explanation: The present simple passive focuses on «the letters».

rounds.prompt: The silver route is not as long as the gold route.

options.text: The routes are the same length.
The gold route is longer than the silver route.
The gold route is not long.

rounds.explanation: «Not as long as» becomes the reverse comparative «longer than».

rounds.prompt: I am sorry that I did not save the confirmation email.

options.text: I wish I would save the confirmation email.
I wish I have not saved the email.
I wish I had saved the confirmation email.

rounds.explanation: A past regret is expressed with «wish I had saved».

rounds.prompt: “I cannot attend because I am ill,” Omar said.

options.text: Omar told that I cannot attend because I am ill.
Omar said that he could attend because he was ill.
Omar said that he could not attend because he was ill.

rounds.prompt: “We have lost the map,” the hikers said.

options.text: The hikers told that we lose the map.
The hikers said me they lost maps.
The hikers said that they had lost the map.

rounds.explanation: The present perfect becomes «had lost» in reported speech.

rounds.prompt: The wind was so strong that the ferry could not leave.

options.text: The wind was not strong enough for the ferry.
The ferry was too strong to leave.
The wind was too strong for the ferry to leave.

rounds.explanation: The result clause becomes an infinitive pattern after «too strong».

rounds.prompt: The green notebook is cheaper than the red notebook.

options.text: The green notebook is more expensive than the red notebook.
The red notebook is more expensive than the green notebook.
The notebooks cost the same.

rounds.explanation: Reversing the comparison changes «cheaper» to «more expensive».

rounds.prompt: “I must leave now,” Dana told us.

options.text: Dana said us that she must left now.
Dana told us that she had to leave then.
Dana said she has to leave yesterday.

rounds.explanation: Obligation changes to «had to» and «now» changes to «then».
